title: Jury selection discussed for trial of Quiboloy co-defendant Felina Salinas
summary: A federal judge and attorneys in Los Angeles discussed jury selection for the trial of Felina Salinas, also known as “Sis Eng Eng,” a Hawaii-based administrator of the Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC).

blocks.text: NEW YORK —A federal judge and attorneys in Los Angeles discussed jury selection for the trial of Felina Salinas, also known as “Sis Eng Eng,” a Hawaii-based administrator of the Kingdom of Jesus Christ (KOJC).

Salinas is a co-defendant of Apollo Quiboloy, founder of the Philippines-based church, in a sex trafficking case in the U.S. District Court for the Central District of California. The court calendar listed Salinas as out on bond.

A 2021 superseding indictment charged Salinas with conspiracy to engage in sex trafficking and multiple substantive counts of sex trafficking. Federal prosecutors allege that she helped recruit girls and young women to serve as Quiboloy’s personal assistants, known as “pastorals,” as part of a scheme to coerce them into sexual acts with him.

At the final status conference, the judge and attorneys discussed trial preparations, including voir dire, the process of questioning prospective jurors to determine whether they can decide the case fairly and impartially.

U.S. District Judge Percy Anderson set noon on Nov. 25, 2026, as the deadline for filing a motion in limine seeking a pretrial ruling on whether or how prosecutors may use a particular photograph at trial. The response is due Nov. 30, 2026.

In June 2020, Salinas pleaded guilty to making a false statement to federal authorities. She had claimed that a cash-filled suitcase aboard a private jet bound for the Philippines was hers. The suitcase reportedly belonged to Quiboloy.

On Feb. 13, 2018, U.S. Customs and Border Protection officers inspected the jet at Honolulu’s Daniel K. Inouye International Airport before its scheduled departure. Salinas declared US$40,000 and 1,000 Philippine pesos.

Officers found about US$40,000 in a red backpack. In a separate carry-on suitcase, they found bundles of cash rolled up inside black socks. The suitcase reportedly contained about US$335,000 and A$9,000.
In October 2020, Salinas was sentenced to 30 days in jail and ordered to pay a $500 fine.—LDF, GMA News
